content:
Webb County voters are showing up in force. Election officials say 3,613 ballots were cast Friday — day five of early voting — pushing the five-day total to 20,637, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The total breaks down to 20,043 in-person votes and 594 mail-in ballots.

Monday was the busiest single day so far with 5,343 ballots, while Thursday was the slowest at 3,301, the Times reported. The Laredo Fire Department Administrative Center led all polling sites with 6,673 votes through five days — 1,125 of them cast on Friday alone.

County Elections Administrator Jose Luis Castillo told KGNS the county is running 20% ahead of the 2022 governor’s race in turnout and participation. Castillo said he expects 40,000 ballots to be cast by the end of early voting, with another 30,000 projected on Election Day.

Site changes are shifting voting patterns this cycle. The Laredo Medical Center location is no longer available, but Castillo said participation at the replacement rehab site is already higher than LMC drew at the same point four years ago. “I’ve looked at the numbers four years ago at LMC as of the present, and we are showing that there is higher participation at the rehab than at LMC,” Castillo told KGNS. He noted LMC used to rank among the county’s top two voting sites before countywide voting freed voters from precinct restrictions.

The ballot carries 38 candidates across 22 contested races at the county, state, and federal levels, plus one proposition, the Times reported. In Texas’ 28th Congressional District, incumbent Democrat Henry Cuellar is seeking a 12th term against Republican challenger and Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina and Green Party candidate Marlon Duran. The Laredo mayoral race fields five candidates: incumbent Dr. Victor Trevino, former councilmember Alfonso “Poncho” Casso, District VIII Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa, customs broker Jose David “JD” Gonzalez, and Jorge Garza. Proposition 1 is a non-binding advisory question asking whether the City of Laredo should support efforts to expand pediatric hospital services in the Laredo–Webb County community; it would not authorize a project, funding, or require county action.

Early voting runs through Friday, Oct. 30. Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 24; noon to 6 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 25; and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26 through Friday, Oct. 30.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “First 5 days of early voting bring more than 20,600 ballots in Webb County,” by Jose De La Rosa, Oct. 23, 2026; KGNS, “Webb County early voting turnout up 20%, official says,” by Ariel Gomez, Oct. 23, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Webb County has banked 20,637 ballots through five days of early voting — up 20% from the 2022 governor's race — with the elections administrator projecting 40,000 early ballots and 30,000 more on Election Day.
title: Early voting sails past 20,600 through day five; Webb County turnout up 20% from 2022
